clue.text: Wife ready to answer question in practice

blocks.note: W is the standard abbreviation for wife
to arm is to make ready for a fight
someone up before a court is there to answer a charge

explanation.surface: A wife stands poised to answer a question during a rehearsal.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is loose: 'up' is used as in 'up before the magistrate', i.e. present to answer questions.
explanation.definitionFit: A warm-up is a preliminary practice session before a match or performance.

clue.text: Nothing out, it's inferred, drained

blocks.note: first meaning: if nothing is out, you infer that everything is in
second meaning: completely exhausted

explanation.surface: Someone deduces that nothing is left outside and feels worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a little logical puzzle: no item out means every item in.
explanation.definitionFit: All in is an informal phrase for utterly exhausted, which is what drained means of a tired person.

clue.text: The best unable to produce striker?

blocks.note: first meaning: without equal, peerless
second meaning: lacking a match, a striker being something struck to make fire

explanation.surface: A football club, however great, cannot find a goalscorer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striker' suggests a footballer; here it is a match that strikes to light.
explanation.definitionFit: Matchless means peerless, without equal, so it describes whatever is the best.

clue.text: First of petty rules for petitions

indicators.note: the opening letter of the following word is all that is taken

blocks.note: the initial letter of petty
to rule over is to lead, and rules is the third-person verb

explanation.surface: A list of small-minded regulations prompts formal requests.
explanation.definitionFit: To plead is to appeal earnestly, so pleads works as the verb petitions.

clue.text: Wrong, how bard might be paid?

blocks.note: first meaning: contrary, unreasonable
second meaning: split as two words, a poet's fee by the stanza

explanation.surface: Someone protests that paying a poet by the line is unjust.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense needs the answer split into Latin 'per' plus 'verse', as in pay per hour.
explanation.definitionFit: Perverse means contrary to what is right or reasonable, so it fits wrong as an adjective.

clue.text: Put the flags out, with pattern done another way

indicators.note: something done another way is rearranged, so these letters take a new order

blocks.note: taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: Bunting is hung for a celebration, with its design arranged differently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Done' looks like part of the indicator but its letters are needed in the fodder; 'another way' alone does the signalling.
explanation.definitionFit: To paint the town red is to celebrate wildly, an idiom akin to putting out flags in festivity.

clue.text: Pasta shapes at origin

indicators.note: as a verb, shapes means moulds into a new form, so the letters are remodelled

blocks.note: taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: Pasta shapes are traced back to where they first came from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pasta shapes' reads as a noun phrase, but 'shapes' is the verb doing the work.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigatoni is a type of ridged tubular Italian pasta.

clue.text: Guillotined, peak figure

indicators.note: a guillotine removes the head, so the front letter goes

blocks.note: a peak is the height or highest point

explanation.surface: A mountain top is sliced off at the summit.
explanation.definitionFit: Eight is a number, and figure is a common word for a numeral.

clue.text: On your bike, drained, hurried to aeroplane

blocks.note: both are curt orders to go away
to bleed is to drain, here in the past tense

explanation.surface: A cyclist, exhausted, rushes to catch a flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On your bike' is British slang for 'go away'. Fighter pilots are said to scramble when they rush to their aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrambled is the RAF term for aircrew rushing to take off quickly, so it means hurried to a plane.

clue.text: Stupid, happy band

blocks.note: blithe means cheerful and carefree
a ring is a circular band

explanation.surface: A foolish, cheerful group of musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' suggests musicians but is a band of metal worn on a finger.
explanation.definitionFit: Blithering is an informal intensifier meaning utterly foolish, as in blithering idiot.

clue.text: Ring road beyond centre of Tangiers

indicators.note: only the middle pair of letters of the named city is kept
placed beyond means coming after, so this part follows the other

blocks.note: the two central letters of the eight-letter name
RD is the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: A ring road runs out past the middle of the Moroccan city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring road' reads as one thing, but 'Ring' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To gird is to encircle or surround, as a ring does.

clue.text: Sharp tooth, end rough

indicators.note: rough suggests something roughed up or not neatly ordered, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: A dentist notes a pointed tooth with a jagged tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp after a time, as in three o'clock sharp, means precisely punctual, just like on the dot.

clue.text: Symbols: children carrying them briefly

indicators.note: one thing carrying another holds it within, so a piece sits inside

blocks.note: tots are small children
'em is the clipped informal form of them

explanation.surface: Little ones lug emblems about, abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an object or emblem serving as a revered symbol of a clan or group.

clue.text: Spots are circling near eyes, originally

indicators.note: originally points to where each word begins, so each opening letter is taken

blocks.note: initial letters of four words

explanation.surface: Blemishes ring the area close to someone's eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: Acne is a skin condition marked by pimples, commonly called spots in Britain.

clue.text: Sour fruit, half of plum eaten by two animals

indicators.note: taking only half of a word means dropping the rest of its letters
something eaten is swallowed inside the eater

blocks.note: the fruit, of which the front half is kept
a crab and an ape

explanation.surface: A tart fruit, half a plum, gets gobbled by a pair of creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the second of the two animals does the eating; the first simply leads the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The crab apple is a small wild apple known for its sharp, acidic taste.

clue.text: Home in tree guarded by blessed good Lord!

indicators.note: what is guarded is surrounded by its guard, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: a bird's home up in a tree
blessed means sacred or holy

explanation.surface: A nest is protected by divine power, praise the Lord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good Lord!' reads as part of the pious scene but is an exclamation of exasperation.
explanation.definitionFit: Honestly! is an exclamation of exasperation, used just like 'Good Lord!'.

clue.text: Signalling plan, heroes excited about that

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters are thrown into a new order
going about something surrounds it, so the stirred word wraps the earlier one

blocks.note: to map out is to plan; a map is a plan
taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: A plan for sending signals has the heroes thrilled.
explanation.definitionFit: Semaphore is a system of signalling with flags held in different positions.

clue.text: Lover of climbing heading for ledge further down

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means going upward, so the short word is read bottom to top
a heading is the top, so only the first letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: taken as written
the initial letter of ledge
lower means further down

explanation.surface: A climber who loves heights moves toward a ledge lower on the face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lover of climbing' reads as one phrase about a mountaineer; 'Lover' is the definition and 'of climbing' is a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower can be an admirer or devotee, close to the sense of a lover or fan.

clue.text: Traveller might have one go left

blocks.note: in cards, to pass is to let your go go by; a pass is a turn
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A tourist may have one more turn remaining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One go left' suggests a last chance; read it as a pass plus port, the nautical left side.
explanation.definitionFit: A passport is the identity document an international traveller carries.

clue.text: Way a little torpedo moves backwards

indicators.note: only a small part of the words is taken, sitting inside them
moving backwards means the letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A small missile travels astern through the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A mode is a manner or method, so it can stand for way as in way of doing things.

clue.text: Wow, group stays part of this?

blocks.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise
a set is a group

explanation.surface: An amazed crowd decides to remain in place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stays' looks like a verb (remains); here it is the noun for the stiffening strips in an undergarment.
explanation.definitionFit: A corset is a tight undergarment shaped by stays, strips of bone or steel sewn into it.

clue.text: Artist in Somme trench, virtually?

indicators.note: virtually means almost entirely, so a word falls just short of complete

blocks.note: the Somme was a great battle of the First World War
a trench is a hole dug in the ground

explanation.surface: A painter is found in a First World War dugout, or almost.
explanation.walkthrough: A war hole is a fair description of a Somme trench; the last letter is dropped. Andy Warhol was the American pop artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Andy Warhol was a celebrated American pop artist, so he is an example of an artist.

clue.text: Religious adherent adopted by Irish in Dublin

indicators.note: something adopted is taken into a household, so the answer lives inside the next words

blocks.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: A believer is taken in by an Irish family in the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindu is a follower of Hinduism, a major religion of India.

clue.text: Massive wicket: dancing!

blocks.note: W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for wicket
hopping about is a lively kind of dancing

explanation.surface: A bowler takes a big wicket and celebrates with a jig.
explanation.definitionFit: Whopping is informal for huge or enormous, a synonym of massive.

clue.text: Known — as is music?

definitions.note: a cryptic description: music is written down in notes

blocks.note: first meaning: famous, well known
second meaning: music is set down in notation

explanation.surface: A familiar tune is recognised by everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Noted means celebrated or famous; music is literally noted, written in notes.

clue.text: Revolution bites back

indicators.note: going back means running the letters the opposite way

blocks.note: nips are small bites

explanation.surface: An uprising strikes back at its oppressors.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin is a single turn or rotation, so it can mean one revolution.

clue.text: Value of prose for poet?

blocks.note: prose is made of words
worth means value

explanation.surface: Someone asks what prose is worth compared with poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Value of prose' becomes 'words' worth', so the pieces read in reverse of the clue order. William Wordsworth was the English Romantic poet.
explanation.definitionFit: William Wordsworth was a major English Romantic poet, so he is an example of a poet.

clue.text: Obligatory paper in colour

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a quire is a measure of paper, 24 or 25 sheets
red is a colour

explanation.surface: A compulsory document printed in a particular shade.
explanation.walkthrough: A quire, 24 or 25 sheets, is an old printer's measure of paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Required means demanded by rule, which is the same as obligatory.

clue.text: Latest tip embraced by judge

indicators.note: something embraced is held within arms, so a piece sits inside another

blocks.note: a tip is an end
to try a case is to judge it

explanation.surface: A judge receives the newest inside information.
explanation.definitionFit: Trendy means fashionable, in line with the latest fashions.
